newsitem.title: MEXICO: Five consortia bid for Mexico natgas distribution.
newsitem.headline: Five consortia bid for Mexico natgas distribution.

text.p: Five international consortia of companies registered formal bids on Thursday for a natural gas distribution permit being auctioned in the main urban center of northern Chihuahua state, Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said Friday in a statement.

Required investment to develop the project could reach $52 million over the next five years, the CRE said. The winning bidder will hold a 30-year operating concession for the region with 12 years of exclusive rights.
Groups vying for the concession are:
--U.S. NorAm Energy and the privately held Mexican firm Corporacion Gutsa ;
--Mexico's Proxima, U.S. Enova Intl. and Pacific Enterprises ;
-- Gas Natural de Latinoamerica and Spain's Repsol ;
--Mexico's Distribuidora de Gas del Norte and U.S. Ensearch Exploration Partners Ltd ;
--Mexico's Triturados Basalticos y Derivados and Public Service Company of New Mexico.
The Chihuahua region is expected to consume more than 600,000 cubic meters per day with consumption rising at least 40 percent in five years, the CRE said.

The CRE said it will review the bids for the Chihuahua region and reject on March 6 those that do not meet its minimum requirements. The winner will be named on March 20, the Energy Ministry said in a statement.

"The permit will be awarded to the bidder that presents a technically feasible project and a sound economic proposal which offers consumers the lowest tariff providing a high quality, safe and efficient service," the CRE said.
"This is the first occasion in which a bidding to distribute energy will imply the transfer of assets from Petroleos Mexicanos," the Energy Ministry said.

Mexico granted natural gas distribution rights in the northern border city of Mexicali, where there was no previous natural gas distribution network. Proxima, Pacific Enterprises and Enova Intl. won the concession.
